title: Agent operation contract
description: A named, versioned operation contract: the provider-neutral definition of one agentic unit of work that a backlog item or initiative can run. It declares WHAT the operation is and requires — its semantic description, required target capabilities, typed caller inputs, typed result fields, the closed set of standard outcomes, evidence expectations, and cancellation/retry semantics — independently of WHICH operating mode implements it. Modes declare implementations; adapters declare capabilities (target-capability.schema.json); bindings choose a mode per target (operation-binding.schema.json). This separation is the whole point of the declarative-operations model: one coherent agentic unit = one operating-mode execution, correlated by a durable domain workflow instance (EXECUTION-MODES.md D4/D5). A contract NEVER names a Go function, service, mode, shell command, or file path — implementation is chosen by binding, not baked into the contract.

version.description: Immutable contract version. Callers pin it; provenance records it. A behavior change is a new version, never an in-place edit.

summary.description: One-line semantic description of the operation.

description.description: Longer operator-facing description of the methodology this operation performs and when it runs.

target_requirements.description: The target capabilities this operation requires. Every bound target kind must provide all of them (checked by CheckOperationTargetCompatibility); a contract that requires only capabilities shared by backlog-item and initiative is reusable across both.

inputs.description: Typed caller inputs the operation accepts. Names are prompt-facing aliases; each declares type, requiredness, and retention. Sensitive inputs may not be retained by value (mirrors the operating-mode caller-input contract).

outcomes.description: The closed set of standard terminal/branch outcomes this operation can report. Bindings and workflow policies route on these; an outcome outside this set is a contract violation.

evidence_expectations.description: Canonical evidence facts a completed operation is expected to have produced, expressed in the same normalized vocabulary as operating-mode evidence requirements (subject_kind + action + min_confidence).

OperationId.description: Kebab-case operation identity — a NOUN-ish behavior name (e.g. review-round, execution-run), never a verb-object target composite (no backlog-item-workshop). Stable once published.

retention.description: How the input is retained for replay. A sensitive input must not use value retention.

ResultSchema.description: The typed structured result an operation execution emits. Fields carry names, types, enums, and requiredness — the same generic field vocabulary the operating-mode resolution ladder validates against.

name.description: Outcome id (e.g. completed, changes-requested, blocked, needs-attention).

disposition.description: How the workflow should treat the outcome. abstain routes to operator attention (never fabricated), matching the operating-mode ladder's needs_attention.

CancellationPolicy.description: Cancellation semantics. cancel_is_cooperative distinguishes a cooperative cancel (the run finishes its current unit and stops) from an abort (immediate). in_flight_disposition records the terminal state a cancelled-in-flight execution lands in.

RetryPolicy.description: Retry semantics. retry_is_new_attempt pins the invariant (INVARIANTS.md Retry-as-New-Attempt) that a retry is a fresh execution parented to the prior one, never an in-place mutation.
